newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P sees Australasian food groups lagging.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P sees Australasian food groups lagging.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday it anticipates creditworthiness of Australasian owned food groups to continue to lag behind foreign-owned food groups. However, the ratings agency said it sees relative earnings stability for the local food industry in the medium term.
"Ongoing rationalisation, cost reduction and increasing branding and marketing activities will be the primarily source of the industry's growth and earnings improvement in the medium term," S&P said.

S&P said while operating peformance of most domestic companies primarily will be driven by domestic earnings in the medium term, offshore expansion will be another alternative to tackle the industry's overcapacity in the long term.
"Standard and Poor's nevertheless views the industry's relative earnings stability as an important element to support the ongoing creditworthiness of food and beverage companies."

"Both cost position and operating performance are expected to improve in the next two years, given the ongoing industrial rationalisation, constant cost reduction, and new competition mentality," S&P said.
S&P said these activities will likely see a fewer number of larger more specialised, and better positioned, companies.
The ratings agency said product and geographic diversification supports the strongest ratings, in the A category, of multinational companies and their Australian subsidaries.

In contrast, operating performance of Australian companies is mainly dependent on the relatively small populations of Australia, 18 million, and New Zealand, 3.5 million, with credit ratings tending to be around the BBB category.
Australia's largest listed food and beverage groups are Goodman Fielder Ltd, Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd, Foster's Brewing Group Ltd, Lion Nathan Ltd and Burns Philip & Co Ltd.
